title: Embedding Layers
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of embedding layers in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of embedding layers and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Embedding Layers: NLP pipelines turn text into token IDs, pad variable-length sequences, and create embeddings or hidden states that a model can process. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Tokenization, padding, masking, and shifted targets define what a language model is allowed to see and what it is trained to predict. For this lesson, focus on nn.embedding and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
embedding = nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=20, embedding_dim=8)
token_ids = torch.tensor([[1, 5, 3]])
print(embedding(token_ids).shape)

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not let a language model attend to future target tokens during autoregressive training or evaluation.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
